activities.title: Alien Engineering Challenge
activities.description: Use paper or clean household objects to design a home for an imaginary alien. Ask what it needs, build together, then explain one design choice.
activities.materials: Paper, pencils; optional clean household objects
activities.adaptations: Practice asking for help and trying a second design.
activities.variations: Shorten the activity, allow passing, or work together instead of competing.

activities.title: Household Scavenger Hunt
activities.description: Agree which rooms and objects are safe to use. Find something soft, something with a pattern and something useful. Share why each was chosen; leave private spaces alone.
activities.adaptations: Take turns giving clues rather than racing.
activities.variations: Shorten the activity, allow passing, or work together instead of competing.

activities.title: Collaborative Tower
activities.description: Build one tower from cups or blocks. Take turns adding pieces and choosing a strategy. If it falls, pause and decide together what to try next.
activities.adaptations: Name frustration and practice a calm restart.
activities.variations: Shorten the activity, allow passing, or work together instead of competing.

activities.title: Emotion Charades
activities.description: Invite each person to choose a feeling and show it through a face or pose. Others offer guesses, then ask what situations could bring that feeling. Passing is welcome.
activities.adaptations: Avoid interpreting someone’s expression as proof of their feelings.
activities.variations: Shorten the activity, allow passing, or work together instead of competing.

activities.title: Cooperative Story
activities.description: Start a story with an imaginary character. Each person adds one sentence. Work together toward an ending; offer a drawing option or a pass.
activities.adaptations: Practice building on another person’s idea before adding your own.
activities.variations: Shorten the activity, allow passing, or work together instead of competing.

activities.title: Paper Airplane Laboratory
activities.description: Fold two paper airplane designs. Choose a safe clear launch area away from faces. Predict which will travel farther, test, then change one feature and test again.
activities.adaptations: Frame unexpected results as information rather than failure.
activities.variations: Shorten the activity, allow passing, or work together instead of competing.

activities.title: Listen and Draw
activities.description: One person describes a simple shape arrangement without showing it. Another draws from the description, asking clarifying questions. Compare kindly and switch roles.
activities.adaptations: Practice checking understanding instead of blaming the speaker.
activities.variations: Shorten the activity, allow passing, or work together instead of competing.

activities.title: Would You Rather
activities.description: Take turns offering lighthearted choices, such as exploring space or the ocean. Share a reason and ask a curious follow-up. Avoid private or distressing topics; passing is fine.
activities.adaptations: Notice different preferences without persuading others to change.
activities.variations: Shorten the activity, allow passing, or work together instead of competing.

activities.title: Mystery Object Detective
activities.description: Choose a safe everyday object. Describe it without naming it while others ask yes/no questions. Reveal it after several guesses and trade roles.
activities.adaptations: Model patient question asking and accepting uncertainty.
activities.variations: Shorten the activity, allow passing, or work together instead of competing.

activities.title: Two Perspectives
activities.description: Invent a mild fictional disagreement, such as two siblings choosing a game. Describe what each character wants, feels and might ask for. Find two possible compromises. Do not require discussion of actual family conflict.
activities.adaptations: Use fictional distance; pause if the scenario becomes uncomfortable.
activities.variations: Shorten the activity, allow passing, or work together instead of competing.
